criteria_results.title: Identifies demand registration threshold deviation (40% vs. 30%)
criteria_results.reasoning: S-1 states the draft's initiation threshold is 40% of Registrable Securities versus 30% in Term Sheet §3.1.

criteria_results.title: Notes 40% threshold was carried over from Series A IRA
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo compares only the Series A start date, minimum size and number of demands. It never says the Series A IRA also used 40% or that the threshold was carried over.

criteria_results.title: Identifies overbroad information rights in Section 3.1(f)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-9 flags §3.1(f) (detailed litigation, regulatory and IP reports, including USPTO and FDA correspondence) as beyond the Term Sheet's four standard deliverables.

criteria_results.title: Flags attorney-client privilege risk from Section 3.1(f)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-9 explicitly states that sharing counsel's assessments generally waives attorney-client privilege and may waive work-product protection.

criteria_results.title: Identifies founder lock-up of 270 days vs. 180-day term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: C-2 identifies the §6.2 Founder-only 270-day lock-up against the Term Sheet's uniform 180 days with no differential.

criteria_results.title: Flags unusually broad scope of founder lock-up (post-IPO option exercises)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-2 notes §6.2 covers after-acquired shares, including shares acquired on option exercise, and says this goes beyond NVCA practice.

criteria_results.title: Identifies 24-month non-compete covenant on founders in Section 7.4
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 describes §7.4's 24-month post-separation worldwide non-compete in synthetic biology, industrial biotechnology and engineered biological systems.

criteria_results.title: Notes non-compete was absent from Series A IRA and term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 cites Term Sheet §5.3 excluding restrictive covenants and the Series A IRA Key Holder page confirming no restrictive covenants.

criteria_results.title: Raises Massachusetts non-compete enforceability concerns
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 analyzes M.G.L. c. 149, §24L, including the 12-month limit and the garden-leave or other consideration requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing QSBS covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: S-12 flags that the draft has no QSBS covenant and proposes commercially reasonable efforts language under IRC §1202.

criteria_results.title: Notes QSBS covenant is market-standard NVCA practice
criteria_results.reasoning: S-12 says a QSBS covenant is now common in NVCA-based documents and cites the NVCA QSBS covenant as the market benchmark.

criteria_results.title: Identifies overbroad ROFO exclusion for strategic partnerships
criteria_results.reasoning: S-8 flags §4.3(g) (strategic partnerships, JVs, licensing, technology development) as overbroad because it lacks the non-capital-raising limit.

criteria_results.title: Notes ROFO carve-out disproportionately benefits CMV via board control
criteria_results.reasoning: S-8 says the carve-out undercuts Northstar's pro rata right. It never ties this to CMV's Board influence or to a disproportionate benefit to CMV.

criteria_results.title: Identifies drag-along missing common stock consent requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: C-3 identifies that §5.1 lets a Preferred majority alone trigger the drag, omitting the Term Sheet's Common majority approval.

criteria_results.title: Notes drag-along deviation gives CMV/Preferred unilateral sale power
criteria_results.reasoning: C-3 explains that CMV plus Verdant alone could drag Northstar, Pinnacle and the Founders, and that the Founders would have no say.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Major Investor threshold of 1,000,000 shares vs. term sheet 500,000
criteria_results.reasoning: C-6 identifies §1.12's 1,000,000-share Major Investor definition against the Term Sheet's 500,000.

criteria_results.title: Identifies internal inconsistency in Major Investor threshold within draft
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo describes §3.5 as a deliberate second tier for 500k-1M holders. It does not flag a conflict between §1.12 and §3.5 as an internal inconsistency.

criteria_results.title: Identifies non-standard audit rights in Section 3.3
criteria_results.reasoning: C-8 flags the Company-paid §3.3 audit at any time on five business days' notice with no frequency or scope limit, against inspection at the investor's expense once a year.

criteria_results.title: Notes audit rights burden on early-stage company with $1.8M/month burn
criteria_results.reasoning: C-8 discusses the cost and finance-team burden for a 47-employee company with a $1.8M monthly burn.

criteria_results.title: Identifies S-3 registration rights not conditioned on eligibility
criteria_results.reasoning: S-2 covers only the $1M minimum and the missing deferral right. It never raises S-3 eligibility or the 'when eligible' language.

criteria_results.title: Notes S-3 language could create contractual impossibility
criteria_results.reasoning: There is no discussion of an obligation to file on Form S-3 before the Company is eligible, or of any contractual impossibility.

criteria_results.title: Identifies termination provision omits Deemed Liquidation Event trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: C-5 states draft §8.1 deletes the Deemed Liquidation Event trigger found in Term Sheet §5.4 and Series A IRA §7.11.

criteria_results.title: Identifies termination consent threshold increased to two-thirds
criteria_results.reasoning: C-5 identifies the consent threshold rising from a majority to two-thirds of Registrable Securities.

criteria_results.title: Identifies board observer rights lack confidentiality obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: C-10 states §6.5 has no confidentiality undertaking for the observer.

criteria_results.title: Identifies board observer rights lack exclusion provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: C-10 states there is no right to exclude the observer and discusses privilege and conflict risks.

criteria_results.title: Notes competitive risk from CMV observer given life sciences focus
criteria_results.reasoning: C-10 notes CMV is a life-sciences-focused fund whose observer could sit on a competitor's board, and C-9 notes CMV's portfolio may include competitors.

criteria_results.title: Issues include specific section references from the draft IRA
criteria_results.reasoning: Every issue in the memo lists specific draft IRA section references.

criteria_results.title: Issues include recommended actions or proposed revisions
criteria_results.reasoning: Each issue includes a recommendation, many with proposed language.

criteria_results.title: Issues are prioritized by severity level
criteria_results.reasoning: Issues are tiered as Critical, Significant and Minor.

criteria_results.title: Drag-along and/or non-compete rated as highest severity
criteria_results.reasoning: Both the non-compete (C-1) and the drag-along (C-3) are rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies the Company as Luminos Biosciences, Inc.
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the company as Luminos Biosciences, Inc.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies CMV as the lead Series B investor / drafter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the draft as prepared by Ashworth Doyle LLP, counsel to Cascade Meridian Ventures, which is the largest Series B investor.

criteria_results.title: Recommends revising demand registration threshold to 30%
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo recommends treating the 40% threshold as a trading chip and conforming to 30% only 'if pressed'. That is not an affirmative recommendation to revise to 30%.

criteria_results.title: Recommends removing or substantially narrowing the non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo recommends deleting §7.4 entirely and its survival.

criteria_results.title: Recommends adding common stock consent to drag-along
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo recommends revising §5.1 to require approval of a majority of the Common, with proposed language.

criteria_results.title: Recommends revising Major Investor threshold to 500,000 shares
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo recommends restoring the 500,000-share threshold in §1.12.

criteria_results.title: Recommends resolving internal inconsistency between Section 1.12 and Section 3.5
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo recommends restoring 500,000 in §1.12 and deleting the §3.5 proviso, which brings the two sections' thresholds into line.
